usages|AABBCC
fields.definition:
* Team index, 0=red, 1=blue
* Player index, 0 through 15
* Race track index, 0 through 31
* Teleporter channel index
* Hill index

fields.name: ctf - flag|AABBCC
fields.definition: Place one flag for each team (usage id)

fields.name: oddball - ball spawn|ABCDCC
fields.definition:
Begin with player index (usage id) set to 0, which will be the first spawn, incrementing up to 15.
They will be spawned incrementally as well.
For best results, 0 should be in a team-neutral location, with each ball located on the opposite side of the map from the previous ball

fields.name: race - track|AABBCC
fields.definition:
These represent the rally points for a lap in race
Begin with track index (usage id) set to 0, incrementing up to 31, leaving no graps in numbers
In rally *MODE*, tracks will be selected at random
For best results, 0 should be in a team-neutral location

fields.name: race - vehicle|AABBCC
fields.definition: Place up to 16 vehicles (usage id is unused)

fields.name: teleport from|ABCDCC
fields.definition: Teleporter entry node. Usage id is used to link entry and exit nodes.

fields.name: teleport to|ABCDCC
fields.definition:
Teleporter exit node. Usage id is used to link entry and exit nodes.
These *DIFFERENCE* between the <facing> value for the entry and exit nodes is added to the player's yaw for their final facing direction upon exit
E.g., assume entry's facing is -90, and exit is 0. That's a difference of +90 (exit minus entry)
The player entrying the teleporter facing north would exit then facing east

fields.name: hill - flag|AABBCC
fields.definition:
Set hill index (usage id) to designate this flag as part that hill. There can only be up to 64 total hills for a map
A hill can consist of up to 12 flags
If a hill consists of only 1 point, it will be 1wu wide in each cardinal direction around the position
The hill represented by index 0 is the default in non-moving hill mode

These fields are only meant to be changed from within Sapien!
Some atom types do not use some fields and may actually show garbage data (or BAD INDEX) here

allow targeting#lets an actor shoot at enemies while following its commands
disable looking#stops an actor from turning, stopping or looking around in response to stimuli received while following its commands

optional#the conversation can continue even if nobody for this participant was found
